solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Commanding officer given roasting about King's Regiment

parts.note: standard abbreviation for a commanding officer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: roasting weather is very hot
R for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An army officer gets a roasting over the state of the King's Regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for Rex, Latin for king; 'about' puts it inside the heat word rather than after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort was a Roman army unit, a tenth of a legion, so a body of soldiers like a regiment.

clue.text: Official essentially supports group of students enduring work

parts.note: a class is a group of students taught together

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of the word, so only its central letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of this eight-letter word

explanation.surface: An official backs a student group that is putting up with its work.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supports' means sits underneath, so the central letters of 'Official' go below the students.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a book, film or piece of music of lasting value, a work that endures over time.

clue.text: As if by magic, Tory sheep scattered

indicators.note: things scattered are thrown about in no order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Conservative supporters vanish like a flock of sheep scattering, as if by magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Hey presto is the conjuror's exclamation when a trick suddenly succeeds, used for anything happening as if by magic.

clue.text: Celebrity regarding present with nonchalance, initially

parts.note: re means regarding or about
the present moment is now

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the word before it, so only its opening letter counts

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A famous person treats a gift with casual indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift, but here it is the present time.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is fame, and celebrity in its abstract sense means the state of being famous.

clue.text: Question a medic working alongside second airborne division

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
QU is a short form of question
taken as written
DR is the abbreviation for doctor
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Interrogating a doctor on duty with a second paratroop unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The S for 'second' comes first even though it is clued last; 'alongside' only says it sits next to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A squadron is an operational unit of an air force, so a division of flying forces.

clue.text: Somewhat short of energy? Give up!

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the following letter is taken away

parts.note: quite means somewhat or fairly
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tired person, running low on energy, tells themselves to stop trying.
explanation.walkthrough: QUITE minus its E leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit is to stop doing something or abandon it, the same as giving up.

clue.text: The French reflected on commonplace consideration

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
a truism is a commonplace, obvious statement

explanation.surface: The French thought about everyday matters and showed thoughtfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the backwards French article sits on top of TRUISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism is selfless concern for others, which is consideration in the sense of thoughtfulness towards people.

clue.text: Rascal chopping ends off shoes

indicators.note: cutting off both ends removes the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: brogues are sturdy leather shoes with decorative perforations

explanation.surface: A rascal snips the toes off someone's shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: BROGUES loses its B and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or mischievous person, a scoundrel or rascal.

clue.text: Crackpot can't use mobile

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so these letters move about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eccentric who cannot operate a mobile phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' reads as a phone, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutcase and crackpot are both informal words for a crazy or eccentric person.

clue.text: Ancient people, say, ran amok

indicators.note: running amok is behaving wildly and out of control, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some ancient tribe, for instance, went on a wild rampage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example', but it is just three letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aryans were an ancient Indo-Iranian people who migrated into Iran and northern India.

clue.text: Incontrovertible report of beneficiary getting drunk

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the next word counts only for its sound

parts.note: an heir is the beneficiary of a will, and the H is silent
tight is informal for drunk

explanation.surface: Firm news that an heir has got drunk on the inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: An airtight argument has no gaps or weak points, so it cannot be disputed.

clue.text: Accepting nothing, impartial journalist partook in competition

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a just judge is fair and impartial
O looks like zero, nothing
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A neutral reporter, taking no bribes, entered a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: JUST takes in O to make JOUST, then ED is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Knights jousted by charging at each other with lances in a tournament, a form of competition.

clue.text: Company enthralled by revolutionary cooking utensil's lid

indicators.note: enthralled means held captive, so one word is held inside another
a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pot is a cooking utensil, and the possessive adds the S
a crew is a company of workers, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A firm captivated by a radical new saucepan lid.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive S on the utensil is part of the reversed word. 'Cooking utensil's lid' wants to be one phrase; only 'lid' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw top is a cap that twists on and off a jar or bottle, a kind of lid.

clue.text: International organisation exposed fakery around announcement of discovery

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards
exposed means stripped of its covering, so the outside letters are removed

parts.note: the European Union
taken as written

explanation.surface: An international body unmasks fraud, as if crying out at a discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exposed' strips both outer letters, not just one, before the remainder is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eureka, Greek for 'I have found it', is the cry Archimedes supposedly gave on discovering his principle.

clue.text: School of Buddhism hits new heights

indicators.note: something new is remade, so these letters take a fresh order

parts.note: Zen is a school of Mahayana Buddhism
these four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A Buddhist school's teachings reach new heights of popularity.
explanation.definitionFit: A zenith is the highest point or peak, so zeniths are high points or heights.

clue.text: Swear copper meets suspects on vacation

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the inside of the word is cleared out and only its outside letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A policeman curses on meeting suspects while away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal; vacation is the American word for a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuss is an informal, chiefly American, form of curse, meaning to use bad language.

clue.text: Old student's conclusion in practical is apparent

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within another word

parts.note: a practical choice is a sensible one

indicators.note: a conclusion is the end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of student

explanation.surface: An ex-pupil's final practical exam seems to be going well.
explanation.walkthrough: The student's last letter goes in after the first letter of the practical word, not at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means seeming to be true on the surface, though perhaps not really so: apparent.

clue.text: Spooner's American sweeties kick Australian native

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words are exchanged

parts.note: sweets are candy in American English; it takes the opening sound of the next word
to kick is to boot; it takes the opening sound of the previous word

explanation.surface: Americans' sweets kick an Australian animal.
explanation.walkthrough: CANDY BOOT with first sounds exchanged becomes BANDY COOT, said like the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandicoot is a small marsupial native to Australia and New Guinea, with a long pointed snout.

clue.text: Uploaded carbon copy account of article exalting India's flatbread

indicators.note: to exalt is to raise up, so in a down entry the article lifts the next letter to sit above it
in a down clue, sent upwards means read from bottom to top, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: CC is the abbreviation for carbon copy
AC is the abbreviation for account
taken as written
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A financial record about an Indian flatbread is posted online.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first three pieces are sent upwards; the article then holds India aloft, which is why India comes before the article in the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Focaccia is a flat Italian bread, usually topped with olive oil, salt and herbs.

clue.text: Expressing remorse, writer holding record within agency retired

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so one word goes within another
retiring is drawing back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: the American Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: within places the combined piece inside the next word

parts.note: a poet is a writer of verse
a log is a written record, as of a voyage

explanation.surface: An author with a criminal record, now out of a government agency, is sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: the record goes inside the writer, and that whole piece goes inside the backwards agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Being apologetic means showing regret or saying sorry, which is expressing remorse.

clue.text: Pilot worked out ratio is below average

indicators.note: something worked out has been processed and rearranged, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: AV is the abbreviation for average
these five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A pilot calculated that a ratio falls below the mean.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'is below' puts the rearranged letters under AV.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a person who flies an aircraft, a pilot.

clue.text: Kiss taken aback by lighting on stage

indicators.note: taken aback suggests being set back, so the letters run from right to left
by here means supplied by, so the letters come from within the words that follow

parts.note: letters spanning the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An actor caught off guard by a kiss under the stage lights.
explanation.walkthrough: SNOG is British slang for a long kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To snog is British slang for kissing passionately, and it is also a noun for such a kiss.

clue.text: Birds finally extending range across river

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word it follows, so only its last letter counts

parts.note: the final letter of this word

indicators.note: a range stretched across something spans it, so one word wraps around a letter

parts.note: the Andes is the mountain range of South America
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Birds at last extend their range across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The ANDES straddle R, and the G goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganders are male geese, so they are birds.

clue.text: Sum doctor charges relative

indicators.note: to charge is to rush into, so the first piece bursts into the middle of the second

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
MO is short for medical officer

explanation.surface: How much a doctor bills a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' reads as billing, but it means the doctor rushes into the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a quantity or total, and sum also means a quantity of money or total.

clue.text: Somehow home and not home

parts.note: someone at home is in
a team not at home plays away

explanation.surface: A paradox of being simultaneously at home and not at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The sporting sense of home and away fixtures supplies the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: In a way means to some extent or after a fashion, close to somehow in the sense of in some manner.

clue.text: Ring after eleven in the morning, it's fundamental

definitions.note: a clause describing the answer: an axiom is something fundamental

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: first letter of AM, the abbreviation for morning, which opens around the rest
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, or a cricket or football team
O is ring-shaped
second letter of AM, closing the container

explanation.surface: Phoning just after eleven in the morning is presented as a basic principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts O behind XI, and the pair goes inside AM for morning: A(XIO)M.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a basic principle taken as self-evident, on which other reasoning is built.

clue.text: Advocate hiding heroin in plant

indicators.note: hiding something means keeping it concealed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: campion is a wild flower with pink or white petals
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A lawyer stashing drugs inside a factory or a pot plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The H goes after the first letter of CAMPION.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to support or speak up for it, which is to advocate it.

clue.text: Oddly withdrawn after the party

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are taken away, so only every other letter is left

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone strangely quiet after the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor celebration or fair, often held to raise money, so a party of a kind.

clue.text: Benevolent witch eruditely entertains visibly nervous individual

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside, so the answer sits within these words

parts.note: letters running from the end of the first word into the start of the third

explanation.surface: A kindly witch is learnedly entertaining a jittery guest.
explanation.walkthrough: Twitcher is usually British slang for a keen birdwatcher; here it is read literally as someone who twitches.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who twitches, making visible nervous jerks, can be called a twitcher.

clue.text: Pelt doormen regularly in commotion

parts.note: an animal's pelt is its fur

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of this word

explanation.surface: Pelting the doormen with things at regular intervals during a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like a verb meaning to throw things, but it is the noun, an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is an outbreak of public anger or excitement, an uproar or commotion.

clue.text: Servant died after farm animal went berserk

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the second, so the clue order is turned round

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a page is a boy servant
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A servant died after a farm animal ran wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the servant and death after the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently and out of control, as if berserk.

clue.text: Condition of artwork European traded with leader of Sioux

indicators.note: trading one thing for another swaps them, so one letter is replaced by a different one

parts.note: a statue is a sculpted work of art
E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the tribal name

explanation.surface: The state of a European artwork swapped with a Sioux chief's.
explanation.walkthrough: The E at the end of STATUE is replaced by S.
explanation.definitionFit: Status means standing or state of affairs, as in condition or position.
